answers.question: I haven't run for two weeks. Do I have to start again from the beginning? And is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?
answers.answer:
**Do you have to start again from the beginning?**

No, but step back a little. Your last blocks were 8 and 9 runs of 2 minutes, and your last run was about two weeks ago. This week uses 6 runs of 2 minutes on Monday and Wednesday, then 5 runs of 3 minutes on Saturday, which brings your running time back close to where it was.

**Is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?**

Finishing the 5K is realistic. Running all 5 km without a walk is a stretch on this timeline, and I would not count on it. Going from 2-minute blocks to about 30 minutes non-stop is a big jump after a break. This is how I would build:

| Week | Longest run without walking | Check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 19 – 25 | 3 min | Three easy runs done |
| Oct 26 – Nov 1 | 8 min | Sat Oct 31: 8 min non-stop at effort 5/10 or less |
| Nov 2 – 8 | 12 min | Two runs, no new distance |
| Nov 9 – 15 | Short easy runs only | Race on Sun Nov 15 |

I recommend planning the race as a run-walk, aiming to run most of it. If you are running 12 minutes non-stop by Nov 8 and feel strong, you can run more of the course without walking. Finishing with walk breaks is a real result, not a failure.

new.analysis:
## What the week showed

The week of Oct 12 – 18 had no runs. All three planned runs were missed, while the four rest days were taken as rest. The week before also had no runs, so three of the last four weeks passed without running.

## Why consistency comes first now

At this stage the biggest gain is getting three runs in each week, not any single hard session. After two weeks off, the body needs a restart rather than a push. Sleep at about 6 hours and high family stress make this harder, so every session this week is easy and short.

## Why there is no quality work

The phase is peak, which normally adds running at race pace. That only works once continuous running is established, and you are not there yet. Your recent runs were moderate effort, not easy, so adding hard work now would raise the chance of another missed week.

## How the restart is built

Your last block was 8 and 9 runs of 2 minutes, about 16 minutes of running. This week has about 12 minutes of running on Monday and Wednesday, then about 15 minutes on Saturday. That rebuilds your running time without asking for more than you have already shown you can do.

## Injury and rest

Stiffness after the drive is not a warning sign by itself. If an ache gets worse during or after a run, stop and have it checked by a qualified professional rather than running through it. Rest days are for recovery, so do not use them to make up missed runs.
